peer_results.rationale: Candidates focus on hardware infrastructure (accelerators, CPUs) and hyperscale cloud adoption, whereas the target focuses on a specific service methodology for Private AI that keeps models close to customer data. While AMD mentions AI workloads, it does not disclose a comparable on-device or data-local privacy strategy.

Candidates discuss hardware launches (Gaudi 3) and broad strategic visions of bringing AI to where data is used, but they do not describe a specific Private AI service model focused on maintaining data control and compliance by moving the model to the data in the same manner as AVGO.

Candidates focus on storage hardware (SSDs, DDR5) required for AI data lakes and high-performance computing workloads. There is no comparable disclosure regarding AI service delivery models or data privacy controls in AI applications.

Candidates focus on the full-stack infrastructure offering (CUDA, GPUs) and regulatory compliance risks related to AI. While NVDA addresses AI infrastructure, it does not disclose a specific Private AI service strategy comparable to AVGO's data-local privacy approach.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization benefits to consumers.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM explicitly prioritize the deployment of AI models directly on the user's device rather than in the cloud to preserve data privacy and control. AVGO’s Private AI service brings the model to the customer's data to avoid compromising control, privacy, and compliance. Similarly, QCOM asserts that generative AI must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing benefits of immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization, contrasting with cloud-centric development.

sentences.text: Advanced services for Private AI provide customers with the benefits of AI without having to compromise control of data, privacy, and compliance by bringing the AI model to customers' data.

While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
